summary: Reconstruct why the September 3 nightly statement emails never went out across the mail relay, message queue, batch scheduler and statement renderer logs; a good answer gives the causal chain in order with log evidence and names the relay certificate rotation that served an incomplete chain (missing intermediate) as the root cause.

findings.what: Change CHG-4471 rotated the outbound mail relay TLS certificate. The calendar gives 21:10 ET on Sep 2, which is 01:10 UTC on Sep 3, matching the relay log reload. The new certificate was loaded with a chain of length 1 instead of 2, i.e. the intermediate (JVB Issuing CA G3 chain) was not served.

evidence.quote: Reload quillmail TLS on mx-relay01 at 21:10.
2026-09-03T01:10:04.120Z mx-relay01 quillmail/tlsmgr[1874]: certificate chain length 1 (previous 2)

findings.counts_if: Answer identifies the relay certificate rotation (CHG-4471) at about 01:10 UTC / 21:10 ET as the start, and says the new certificate was deployed without the intermediate / with an incomplete chain (chain length 1 vs 2).

findings.what: From 01:12 UTC the mailer workers (mailer-1, mailer-2) that consume the email queues can no longer complete STARTTLS with the relay: the relay sees unknown_ca alerts and the consumers report x509 certificate signed by unknown authority. Other relay clients and the ops-jump01 post check still succeed, which is why the change looked fine.

evidence.quote: 2026-09-03T01:12:47.530Z mx-relay01 quillmail/smtpd[2211]: TLS handshake failed from mailer-1.jvb.internal[10.40.12.21]: peer sent alert unknown_ca (48)
"last_error": "smtp starttls mx-relay.jvb.internal:587: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
A-77339,NotifyDeadLetterNonEmpty,warning,message-queue,notify.email.dlq,2026-09-03 01:52:40,,open,dead letter queue depth above 0

findings.counts_if: Answer says the mailers could not send because TLS to the relay failed certificate verification (unknown CA / untrusted certificate) after the rotation. Grading note (accepted, not required): also noting that the notify.email.send queue failed the same way (first unknown authority error 01:12:48, a message dead-lettered at 01:52, alert A-77339 NotifyDeadLetterNonEmpty still open) strengthens the answer, as does saying the outage was still unresolved by morning (mailer handshakes still failing at 08:54).

findings.what: Statement messages published by the renderer from 01:30 UTC are never acknowledged; the stmt.email.send queue policy retries without limit, so messages are redelivered over and over and the queue backs up (ack_rate 0, ready count climbing to about 36,000).

evidence.quote: {"ts": "2026-09-03T01:31:40.662Z", "node": "lq-2", "level": "warn", "msg": "message redelivered", "queue": "stmt.email.send", "consumer": "mailer-2", "attempt": 3,
"max_delivery_attempts": "unlimited"

findings.counts_if: Answer says the failed sends were retried/requeued so stmt.email.send accumulated messages (nothing acknowledged) instead of draining.

findings.what: At 02:47:13 UTC broker node lq-2 hit its memory high watermark (the backlog of PDF-carrying messages) and blocked the renderer's publishing connection; the renderer logs the block and stops at 36,114 of 41,862 statements.

evidence.quote: "msg": "memory high watermark reached, blocking publishers"
time=2026-09-03T02:47:14.019Z level=warn component=publisher msg="broker blocked connection" reason="resource alarm: memory" conn=stmt-render@bat-app04:51344

findings.counts_if: Answer links the queue backlog to a broker memory alarm around 02:47 UTC that blocked the renderer from publishing, stalling the batch.

findings.what: With progress stuck at 36114/41862, the Tidewell job STMT_NIGHTLY (run 88213, maxrun 3h from 01:30) exceeded its maximum runtime at 04:30 UTC and was sent SIGTERM; STMT_ARCHIVE_PUSH was skipped.

evidence.quote: [2026-09-03 04:30:00 UTC] ERROR job=STMT_NIGHTLY run=88213 exceeded maxrun 3h00m, sending SIGTERM to pid 40517

findings.counts_if: Answer says the scheduler killed/timed out the statement job at 04:30 UTC because it exceeded its 3 hour max runtime while blocked.

findings.what: On SIGTERM the renderer aborted, marked batch B-20260903 FAILED and, per its on_abort=purge_outbound setting, purged the 36,114 queued statement emails, so none were delivered (delivered_confirmed=0).

evidence.quote: time=2026-09-03T04:30:04.006Z level=error component=batch msg="batch failed" batch=B-20260903 state=FAILED reason=terminated published=36114 purged=36114 delivered_confirmed=0
"msg": "queue purged", "queue": "stmt.email.send", "messages": 36114

findings.counts_if: Answer says the renderer marked the batch failed and the queued messages were purged, so zero statement emails were sent (not a partial send).

exclusions.what: PDF signing latency spike and hsm-a failover on the renderer (alert A-77338), from planned HSM maintenance CHG-4472.

evidence.quote: A-77338,RendererSigningLatencyHigh,warning,statement-renderer,bat-app04,2026-09-03 01:41:30,2026-09-03 01:58:30,auto,PDF signing p95 above 1500 ms
msg="hsm-a returned 503 maintenance, failing over" target=hsm-b.jvb.internal

exclusions.why_not: Planned maintenance; signing only slowed for 17 minutes, auto-resolved at 01:58, and rendering and publishing continued at full rate afterwards until the broker block at 02:47.

exclusions.what: Lanternq peer lq-3 unreachable at 23:48 UTC on Sep 2 (alert A-77335).

evidence.quote: A-77335,LanternqPeerUnreachable,critical,message-queue,lq-3,2026-09-02 23:48:32,2026-09-02 23:51:10,auto,cluster peer lq-3 missed heartbeats for 30s

exclusions.why_not: A switch link flap on a different node that recovered in under 3 minutes, before the rotation and before the batch started; the statement queue lives on lq-2.

evidence.quote: [2026-09-03 02:00:41 UTC] ERROR job=GL_RECON run=88106 stderr: input file /data/inbound/gl/GLX_20260902.dat not found

exclusions.why_not: Unrelated general ledger job waiting on a late input file; its retry succeeded at 02:49 and it has no dependency relationship with STMT_NIGHTLY.

exclusions.what: CHG-4466 Tidewell scheduler agent patch listed for Sep 2 22:00 ET.

evidence.quote: **CHG-4466** · Tidewell scheduler: patch agents on bat-app01 to bat-app04 to 5.2.1

exclusions.why_not: It was postponed to Sep 10 and never happened, so it cannot explain the scheduler timeout.

exclusions.what: CHG-4473 branch DNS forwarder replacement and CHG-4464 cards-default TTL change on the same day.

evidence.quote: - Affects: branch LAN name resolution only. Data center resolvers unchanged.
- Affects: queues bound to `cards-default` only (card authorization events). No other policies touched.

exclusions.why_not: Changes on other systems/scopes: branch DNS does not serve the data center batch path, and the TTL change only touched the card authorization policy, not stmt.email.send.

exclusions.what: Relay spool disk above 80% at 03:20 UTC (alert A-77343) and other relay noise (dnsbl timeouts, printer relay rejects).

evidence.quote: A-77343,RelaySpoolDiskHigh,warning,mail-relay,mx-relay01,2026-09-03 03:20:00,2026-09-03 03:42:30,auto,/var/spool/quillmail above 80%

exclusions.why_not: Happens every night around 03:20 (same alert on Sep 2 when statements went out fine) and clears after log compression; it started long after sends were already failing.

exclusions.what: Lanternq management listener certificate expiring soon (alert A-77297, queue log warning).

evidence.quote: A-77297,LanternqMgmtCertExpiry,warning,message-queue,lq-2,2026-08-30 06:00:00,,open,management listener certificate expires in 45 days

exclusions.why_not: A certificate that has not expired, on the broker's management listener, not the relay certificate the mailers failed to verify.

exclusions.what: Renderer warnings: deprecated footer template, font fallback, GC pauses, accounts skipped for no email on file.

evidence.quote: msg="template footer_v6 is deprecated, footer_v7 available" template=retail_monthly

exclusions.why_not: Normal per-account and JVM noise, unrelated to publishing.

exclusions.what: CHG-4476 data warehouse partition change with a 01:00 to 01:15 window on Sep 3, which lines up with the 01:10 failures only if the ET window is misread as UTC.

evidence.quote: **CHG-4476** · Data warehouse: add nightly partition for `txn_fact_2026_09`
**All times below are US Eastern (EDT, UTC-4) unless stated otherwise.**

exclusions.why_not: The window is 01:00 to 01:15 ET, which is 05:00 to 05:15 UTC, after the batch had already failed; it is also on the data warehouse, not in the statement email path.

answer.value: Root cause: CHG-4471, the TLS certificate rotation on outbound mail relay mx-relay01 at 01:10 UTC (21:10 ET Sep 2), installed the new certificate without its intermediate (chain length 1 instead of 2). The mailer workers could not verify it (unknown CA), so every statement email failed, was retried without limit, backed up stmt.email.send until broker lq-2 hit its memory alarm at 02:47 and blocked the renderer, the scheduler killed STMT_NIGHTLY at its 3 hour maxrun at 04:30, and the renderer failed the batch and purged all 36,114 queued emails.
answer.derivation: changes.md places the relay reload at 21:10 ET = 01:10 UTC; the relay log shows chain length 1 (previous 2) at 01:10:04 and the first mailer unknown_ca failure at 01:12:47; the queue log shows x509 unknown authority redeliveries with unlimited attempts, a memory watermark block of stmt-render at 02:47:13 and a purge of 36114 messages at 04:30:03; the renderer log shows the block at 02:47:14 and the FAILED batch with delivered_confirmed=0; the scheduler log shows maxrun exceeded at 04:30:00. The ops-jump01 post check and other relay clients still succeeding explain why the rotation was marked Completed.
answer.counts_if: Names the relay certificate rotation with an incomplete chain / missing intermediate (not merely 'the relay' or 'the queue memory alarm' or 'the scheduler timeout') as root cause.

mistakes_that_matter: Naming the queue memory alarm, the scheduler maxrun timeout or the renderer failure as the root cause; they are downstream symptoms and fixing them (raising the watermark or maxrun) would not have sent a single email.
Blaming the HSM signing latency, the lq-3 peer flap, GL_RECON or the postponed Tidewell patch.
Saying some statement emails went out (partial send); all 36,114 published messages were purged and the remaining 5,748 were never rendered.
Misreading the change calendar times as UTC and concluding the rotation happened hours away from the failures, or ruling it out because its post check passed.
Recommending a rerun without fixing the relay certificate chain, which would fail the same way.
